newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers shorten US debt portfolios - MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers shorten US debt portfolios - MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers shortened the durations of their U.S. debt portfolios in the week ended March 17, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"Weighted durations fell ... and cash positions rose significantly, consistent with (the) market back up," according to MCM first vice president and senior economist Astrid Adolfson.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark fell to 107.0 percent from 107.8 percent the week before.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 39 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," compared with 27 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" fell to 8.0 percent, down from 9.0 percent in the week ended March 10.
Fifty-three percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 64 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 3.26 percent, against 3.10 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 33 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 31 percent the previous week, while 9.0 percent underweighted it. The remaining 58 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 48 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 16 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
